decision.summary: The gas safety certificate for 19 Victoria Park Road is valid until 16 October 2026, so the property is compliant today. The tenant has not replied to emails or SMS, so I sent a further SMS and email, emailed the landlord, opened JOB-101, set a 12 October review, and escalated to compliance (ESC-108) in case access cannot be arranged before expiry.

answers.question: 1. Is the property currently compliant for gas safety? Which record do you trust and why?
answers.answer: Yes, for now. The CP12 issued 2025-10-17 by Gas Safe engineer 550123 expires 2026-10-16, and today is 2026-10-10. I trust compliance.json, the current system record with the signed CP12 file reference. The legacy note 'gas cert renewed 2025' agrees but is hearsay and was only used as support. Compliance lapses after 2026-10-16 unless a new CP12 is issued.

answers.question: 2. What steps do you take to get access lawfully before expiry?
answers.answer: Opened JOB-101. Sent tenant an SMS and an email asking for a visit time this week, with 24h written notice and an alternative if he can't be home. Set a review for 2026-10-12. If there is no reply, a formal 24h written access notice is the next step, with the visit booked with HeatRight Ltd before 2026-10-16. Entry without notice or consent is not allowed. Escalated to compliance (ESC-108) for a decision on formal notice.

answers.question: 3. What do you tell the landlord?
answers.answer: Emailed Ben Hartley: the CP12 is valid today and expires 2026-10-16; the tenant has not replied; HeatRight (his preferred contractor) will be booked once access is confirmed or notice is given; the price is not yet known and nothing over £300 including VAT will be committed without his approval.
